title: fix(guards): the Bash doors read a multi-line command, a heredoc and an unbalanced quote

evidence.value: six doors pass a command on a second line on main 5d7157b; the same scanner also refused a builder's python3 heredoc edit script at 08:29:20 today (a false positive the branch already fixes)
evidence.time: the bypass is described in public on issue #1068 since this morning and main still carries it; each day main moves, the parked branch needs another rebase
evidence.risk: closes the newline, heredoc and unreadable-command bypasses on six doors; the fail-closed flag closes seven inputs that pass on main or the branch, all checked against real bash 5.2
evidence.size: builds on claude/1068-guards-multiline at 7fd4019: it merges cleanly onto main 5d7157b (3000 lines, 328 passed); the spike changed two lines of _lines and every existing guards test still passed

promise: Resume the parked branch claude/1068-guards-multiline at 7fd4019 (rebase or merge onto main; it merges cleanly onto 5d7157b). Keep everything that passed there: a newline outside quotes ends a command, backslash-newline continuations join, heredoc bodies are read in order, an unreadable command naming a door program is refused, and the refusal names --body-file and -F. Replace the arithmetic depth counter in guards._lines with a one-way flag. The flag is set at the first unquoted '((' (which also covers '$(('), at '${', or at a '[' joined to the character before it ('$[', 'a[', '(['). Once it is set, no later heredoc body is dropped; the rest of the command is read as commands, which fails closed. '))' is no longer tracked, so no paren shape can reopen body dropping. The pattern goes inline, so the flag takes the two lines the depth branch held (net 0 against the branch; a spike with a separate constant came to 3001). Accepted cost: a heredoc whose body names a door program after an arithmetic or parameter expansion is refused (1 of 506 real commands today, a sentinel's probe script). Option (b), the paren stack, is not taken: a case pattern's unmatched ')' and the bracket forms ${...}, $[...] and a[...] each need their own modelling, and a stack that mis-pops reopens body dropping, which is the failure class of both fix rounds. Touches cli/wuwei/guards.py (_lines, the docstring) and tests/test_guards.py, with the branch's existing hook.py and spec files. Outside: python -c and other interpreter bodies, here-strings, eval, input piped to a shell, compound bodies, shell flags before -c and wrapper options (item compound-doors), any new door.
acceptance: given 'true\ngit push --force origin x', when the Bash door reads it, then the force-push door refuses

it's done
EOF
gh pr create -F b.md" and the gates missing at the branch head, when the Bash door reads it, then the create door reads the create and refuses

git push --force origin x
EOF]', 'x=2; echo ${x:1<<EOF }
git push --force origin x

git push --force origin x

git push --force origin x

title: fix(ws): a ledger line that is not a well-formed row is skipped by every reader

evidence.value: found by a gate, not in real use: the 1065 doctor gate found that {"kind":[1]} stops doctor (setup.py:151 builds a set from kind); ws._parse keeps any JSON value (ws.py:121-128)
evidence.time: no trigger seen in today's ledger; only a hand edit or a bad sync writes such a line
evidence.risk: by reading hook.py:75-84 and ws.py:143-145: when this clone's last ledger line is a non-object or an object without a hash, ws.record raises, hook.handle fails open, and a refusal the guards returned never reaches the harness, so every door passes (not run: the ledger door refused my probe, correctly)
evidence.size: about five lines in ws.py plus tests; ws.traces can reuse _parse and free more than that

promise: ws._parse keeps only well-formed rows: a JSON object whose ts and kind, where present, are strings and whose data, where present, is an object. ws.record chains to the hash of the last row that has one, so a malformed last line never raises. ws.ledger(), ws.rows() and doctor's hooks check read only kept rows, and ws.verify() still reports every malformed line by file:line. Touches cli/wuwei/ws.py (_parse, record), cli/wuwei/setup.py (line 151 drops its own isinstance filter) and tests. Lines: ws.traces (ws.py:178-189) re-implements the parse loop and can call _parse, which frees about five lines against the two added. Outside: the ledger format, sync, the ledger door.
acceptance: given this clone's ledger file ending in a line '[1]', '5', 'null' or '{"a": 1}', when ws.record appends a row, then it raises nothing and the new row's prev is the hash of the last row that has one
given a ledger file holding '{"kind": [1]}', '{"ts": 5, "kind": "x"}' and a row whose data is a list, when ws.ledger(), ws.rows() and doctor run, then each finishes and skips those lines
given the same file, when ws.verify() runs, then it still names each malformed line by file:line
given the change, when the suite runs, then the runtime size test still passes at 3,000 lines or fewer
why: A non-object or hashless last ledger line makes ws.record raise. By reading the code, a refusal is then lost to the hook's fail-open, so every door passes. One change to _parse fixes record, ledger(), rows() and doctor.

given a call the guards refuse and ws.record raising (the ledger directory read-only, or a malformed last ledger line), when PreToolUse runs, then the deny still reaches the harness

title: fix(guards): the doors read a command inside a loop or if body, after shell flags, and after a wrapper's options

evidence.value: on main, the guards pass every one of these (probed in a scratch copy): for/while/if/else bodies, '{ ...; }', '! cmd', 'bash -lc' and 'sh -ec', 'timeout 60', 'nice -n 10' and 'env -u X'. They are shapes a cooperating agent writes: 97 of 506 commands today used for/while loops, 35 used if, 7 used shell flags before -c, and 1 used timeout
evidence.time: no door appeared inside a compound body or behind a wrapper in today's commands (the only hit was my own probe), and the gaps are already listed in the public 1068 security verdicts
evidence.risk: closes the gaps a cooperating agent plausibly writes; SECURITY.md calls the guards cooperative mistake prevention, so eval, input piped to a shell, here-strings, a variable as the program and $(...) inside double quotes stay out as residual

title: fix(hook): a gate's verdict is linted before its hand-back, and a stop that cannot block records verdict.missing

evidence.value: 1067's quality and arch verdicts at 3fb3f40 have no attest and no verdict.missing row. The quality seat's transcript shows SubagentStop blocked at 08:41:31 with the shape error after SubagentHandback had already ended the run, so the seat never rewrote it and the coordinator had to resume it by hand
evidence.time: every gate run in auto mode ends with SubagentHandback, so each malformed verdict is lost the same way
evidence.risk: G-1 measures gates attested at the head; a lost attest shows as a missing gate. Padding: 4 findings in today's verdicts carry made-up ':1' anchors, one pointing at a directory
evidence.size: a PreToolUse check of SubagentHandback (about four lines), one record moved, one regex group made optional; post_tool's hand-back re-read (hook.py:205-212) folds into it

promise: The SubagentStop lint and evidence's lint are already one check (both call verdict.parse; hook.py:179, evidence.py:10). The gap is timing: SubagentHandback ends the seat's run, so a block from SubagentStop lands after the seat can act, and nothing is recorded because no second stop comes. Fix: (1) PreToolUse on SubagentHandback lints the verdict file named by the message's 'Verdict file:' line with the same _verdict_problem. It denies the hand-back with the shape errors and the format, so the seat rewrites before its run ends. When the verdict is well formed it records the attest there. (2) SubagentStop records verdict.missing for a problem whenever it cannot block to effect: on stop_hook_active as today, or when the hand-back has already ended the run. (3) verdict.parse accepts a non-blocking finding without a file:line ('- [low] blocks: no. <note>'); a blocking finding still needs file:line and 'Failure:'. The sentinel charters and FORMAT say so, so no seat pads ':1' anchors. Touches cli/wuwei/hook.py (pre_tool, subagent_stop, post_tool), cli/wuwei/verdict.py (FINDING, FORMAT), the sentinel charters with a rebuilt agents/, and tests. Lines: post_tool's Agent hand-back re-read (hook.py:205-212, 7 lines) goes, because the hand-back check reads the same message earlier. Outside: evidence's verdict counting, the verdict file location.
acceptance: given a sentinel seat calls SubagentHandback with a message ending 'Verdict file: .wuwei/verdicts/1067/quality-3fb3f40.md' and that file holds a finding line with no file:line and no blocks:, when PreToolUse runs, then the hand-back is denied with the shape errors and the format
given the same hand-back with a well-formed verdict, when PreToolUse and then SubagentStop run, then exactly one attest row is recorded for that file
given a seat whose run already ended by hand-back and a verdict problem found at SubagentStop, when the hook runs, then a verdict.missing row is recorded with the problem

given '- [low] blocks: no. a note on the design', when verdict.parse reads the findings, then it is accepted as a non-blocking finding; given '- [high] blocks: yes. Failure: x', then it is rejected for its missing file:line
given the change, when the suite runs, then the runtime size test still passes at 3,000 lines or fewer
why: A malformed gate verdict is blocked only after the hand-back has ended the seat's run, so it is neither fixed nor recorded (1067's quality verdict at 3fb3f40). Linting at the hand-back fixes the timing, and seats stop padding ':1' anchors.
